beliefs.practice: Validate and enforce a single fixed embedding dimensionality for the collection (e.g., 1536) before creating a vector index and reject or migrate any documents with a different embedding shape.
Create the vector index (HNSW/DiskANN/IVF) with the exact embedding dimension and algorithm parameters before ingesting vector documents to avoid incompatible-index errors.
Store the connection string/URI outside source control (environment variable or Azure Key Vault) and never log or write the live DOCUMENTDB_URI value to files or test fixtures.
Use a least-privilege database user account for the sample (grant read/write only to sample_healthcare_13) instead of the cluster admin/root credentials.
Reuse a single MongoClient across the app (application-level client) with appropriate pool settings (maxPoolSize) rather than creating a new client per request; close it cleanly on shutdown.
Enable TLS/SSL with server certificate validation in the connection string (tls=true, tlsAllowInvalidCertificates=false or equivalent) to protect PHI in transit.
Keep embedding generation deterministic or versioned (include an embedding_version field) so previously-indexed profiles remain comparable when model or dimension changes occur.

Prefer server-side vector search (e.g., $search or the provider's vector operator) using the vector index for nearest-neighbor retrieval; fall back to client-side cosine only when server support or index is unavailable.
Before tuning/creating indexes, run explain() on representative queries (including $search) and verify index usage with the cluster's tools to avoid missing or inefficient indexes.
Instrument and monitor slow queries and vector search latency (APM/metrics) and capture index build and query plan warnings to guide index parameter tuning.
Implement validation logic on ingest to ensure embedding arrays are numeric (float32/float64), within expected length, and free of NaN/Inf; reject or normalize invalid data before persisting.

If you must change the embedding dimensionality or vector index algorithm, create a new collection or namespace (or re-index after removing incompatible documents) instead of trying to change an existing incompatible index in-place.
Use exponential backoff and jitter for retries on transient errors (network glitches, 5xx, rate limits) and make write operations idempotent (upsert with unique keys or idempotency tokens).
Set appropriate writeConcern and readPreference for the workload (e.g., majority writeConcern for critical PHI writes, local reads for low-latency noncritical queries) and document these tradeoffs.
Choose a partition/shard key that avoids hot partitions for retrieval patterns (for example, use clinic_id or a hashed patient_id rather than a monotonically increasing field).
Tune vector index parameters (HNSW's m and efConstruction, efSearch or DiskANN config) to balance recall vs latency and record the values used so experiments are reproducible.
Limit returned documents and fields (projection) when retrieving similar profiles: return only ids, scores, and essential metadata unless embeddings are necessary for client-side reranking.
Protect patient data: enable encryption at rest in the managed cluster, enable auditing, and consider client-side field-level encryption for direct identifiers before storing them in the cluster.

When seeding sample or synthetic patient profiles, keep them isolated in the sample_healthcare_13 database/collection and provide a .env.example placeholder rather than real credentials or real PHI in tests or fixtures.
Use deterministic offline embedding and agent fallbacks for unit tests to avoid hitting external LLM/embedding services, and assert retrieval logic independently from upstream model availability.
Avoid storing raw LLM API keys in the same store as DB credentials; rotate keys regularly and use Key Vault/managed identities for service-to-service secrets where possible.
When creating indexes or performing heavy ingestion, run those operations in off-peak windows and monitor the cluster resource usage because vector index builds can be resource intensive.
Implement TTL indexes for ephemeral records (e.g., temporary agent memory or session embeddings) to control storage growth and comply with retention policies.

When vector server-side search isn't available, fetch a limited candidate set using inexpensive filters (metadata, coarse similarity) and only compute client-side cosine on that subset to control CPU/memory.
